title: ENG-205 Midsummer Act 5 — 1 Main Ideas Pathway (play in order)
subject: ENG-205

cards.def: After Puck's love-juice mixups and Bottom's night as an ass, Oberon has the changeling boy, Titania is released, Lysander again loves Hermia, and Demetrius remains true to Helena. Theseus overbears Egeus, the three couples are to be married in the temple, and the mechanicals, with Bottom safely home, prepare the play they hope will be "preferred."

cards.term: 1. The lunatic, the lover, and the poet
cards.def: Because the lovers' night sounds unbelievable, Theseus groups the lunatic, the lover, and the poet as "of imagination all compact," but Hippolyta answers that their shared story grows to "something of great constancy."

To wear away the three hours between after-supper and bedtime, Theseus rejects other shows and chooses the mechanicals' "tedious brief" "tragical mirth," saying nothing can be amiss when simpleness and duty tender it.

cards.term: 3. A prologue that misses its points
cards.def: Quince's prologue comes out disordered because he "doth not stand upon points," after which the tradesmen present Wall, Moonshine, and Lion and tell the whole Pyramus and Thisbe plot before they act it.
Bottom as Pyramus and Flute as Thisbe play the deaths at "Ninny's tomb" so clumsily that the court laughs, and Theseus refuses their epilogue and asks for a Bergomask dance instead.

At midnight Theseus sends the lovers to bed because it is "almost fairy time," Oberon and Titania bless the three couples, and Puck tells the audience to think the play a dream if the "shadows" have offended.
